en.title: Maximum Number of Fish Caught
en.description:
Every fish and every bait has a positive integer size. A bait must be strictly smaller than a fish to catch it; each bait can be used at most 3 times, and each fish can be caught at most once. Find the maximum number of fish that can be caught.

The input protocol and the examples in this batch were compiled by CSWork.
en.input: The first line contains n m (1..100000); the second line contains n fish sizes, and the third line contains m bait sizes, all values in 1..10^9.
en.output: Output the maximum number of fish caught.
en.explanation: Process according to the definite rules above; see the accompanying editorial for the approach, proof of correctness, and complexity.
hints: Sort fish and baits from smallest to largest. For each bait, skip fish no larger than it, then use it to catch up to three of the smallest catchable fish currently left.
